summary: Converts PDFs and other documents to clean Markdown, JSON or HTML quickly, keeping tables, equations and images.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Marker converts documents to Markdown, JSON, chunks and HTML quickly and accurately. It handles PDF, image, PPTX, DOCX, XLSX, HTML and EPUB files in all languages, formats tables, forms, equations, links and code blocks, extracts images and removes headers and footers.
sixtySeconds.problem: Getting clean text out of PDFs for AI pipelines or notes is hard. Marker produces structured output that LLMs and RAG systems can use.
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for fast, accurate conversion with several speed and accuracy modes, a GUI, batch processing and an agent skill.
requirements: A GPU helps for the balanced and vllm modes

overview: Install with pip install marker-pdf, or marker-pdf[full] for non-PDF formats. Convert one file with marker_single, a folder with marker, or open a browser GUI with marker_gui.

Modes: no_ocr uses the PDF's text layer, fast (default on CPU and Apple Silicon) uses ONNX OCR, balanced (default on GPU) routes hard pages to VLM OCR, and vllm runs full-page VLM OCR. Use --output_format to choose markdown, json, html or chunks.
The code is Apache 2.0. The model weights use a modified AI Pubs Open Rail-M license, free for research, personal use and startups under a revenue limit, so check it before commercial use.
limitations: Model weights have their own license limits
Best accuracy modes want a GPU
